{16} ﴿So how was My punishment and warning?﴾, meaning: how did you see, O addressee, the painful punishment of Allah and His warning, which leaves no proof for anyone against it?

For this reason Allah calls His servants to turn to it and to remember, by His saying: ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾

{23} That is: **"Thamud denied"** (the warners). They were the well-known tribe in the land of al-Hijr, who denied their Prophet Salih, peace be upon him, when he called them to worship God alone, without partner, and warned them of punishment if they opposed him.

{24} They denied him, behaved arrogantly toward him, and said out of pride and self-conceit: **"Shall we follow a single human being from among us?"** That is: how can we follow a mere human being rather than an angel, and one from among us rather than from others who are greater in people's eyes than we are? And even so, he is only one person. **"Then indeed we would be in error and madness"**, that is: if we followed him in this condition, we would be misguided and wretched. This speech was part of their own error and wretchedness, for they disdained to follow a messenger from among mankind, yet they did not disdain to worship trees, stones and images.

{25–26} **"Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?"** That is: how does God single him out from among us and send down the Reminder to him? What distinction has he been given over us? This was an objection from the deniers against God, by which they kept showing off, asserting themselves [and evading], and rejecting the call of the messengers. God answered this doubt through the words of the messengers to their peoples: **"Their messengers said to them, 'We are only human beings like you, but God bestows His favour upon whomever He wills among His servants.'"** So God bestowed upon the messengers qualities, characters and perfections by which they became fit for the messages of their Lord and for being singled out for His revelation. It is part of His mercy and wisdom that they were human; for had they been angels, mankind could not have received from them, and had He made them angels, He would have hastened punishment upon those who denied them. The purpose of this speech from Thamud to their Prophet Salih was to deny him, and for this reason they passed this unjust judgment upon him, saying: **"Rather, he is a liar, an insolent one!"** That is: one who lies greatly and does much evil! So may God disfigure them, how foolish their minds were, how wrongful, and how harsh they were in answering the truthful, sincere advisers with such vile speech.

He sent the she-camel, which was among the greatest of blessings upon them, as a sign and a favour from God; they would milk from her what sufficed all of them. **"As a trial for them"**, that is: a test and an examination from Him. **"So watch them and be patient"**, that is: persevere in your call to them and await what will befall them, or await whether they will believe or disbelieve.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 54, verses 33–40:

{33–40} That is: {The people of Lut denied the warners} — Lut (peace be upon him) when he called them to worship Allah alone, without partner, and forbade them from shirk and from the abomination that no one among the worlds had committed before them. But they denied him and persisted in their shirk and their vile deeds. So much so that the angels who came to him in the form of guests, when his people heard of them, came hastening, intending to commit the abomination upon them — may Allah curse and abhor them — and they solicited him to surrender his guests. So Allah commanded Jibril (peace be upon him), and he obliterated their eyes with his wing. Their Prophet warned them of Allah's seizure and punishment. {So they disputed the warnings.} {And certainly a lasting punishment came upon them early in the morning.} He overturned their dwellings, made its lowest part its highest, and pursued them with stones of baked clay, layered, marked in the presence of your Lord for the transgressors. Allah saved Lut and his family from the great distress, as a reward for their gratitude to their Lord, their worship of Him alone without partner.
